why_this_track: 35% of every dollar PK has earned - $21.15 of $61.39 - on 212,000 plays, and the only track with a proven audience. That audience is Filipino and it found the song through other people's Reels using the audio, not through PK's own posts. The flagship video belongs to the song people already found.
premise: Bayanihan is the Filipino tradition of a whole neighbourhood physically lifting a house and carrying it to new ground. The song is about that: nobody is left behind, walang iwanan. So the film is one long accumulation - a single figure, alone, joined by one more, then a handful, then a crowd, until the frame cannot hold them and the thing they carry is airborne.
spine: COUNT. Where The Cave's spine is light, this one's is how many silhouettes are in frame: 1 → 2 → 4 → 12 → too many to count → and at the very end, one again, but now part of a line stretching past the edges. If a viewer with the sound off can feel the frame filling, the story worked.
character_note: The locked Wanderer is a SOLITARY figure, which fights a song about community - so the constraint becomes the theme. Every additional person is the SAME silhouette: same deep hood, same ground-length hem, same squared shoulders, all back-to-camera. Not a crowd of strangers, a crowd of him. That is what makes it read as one people rather than extras.
palette_note: Same monochrome teal-and-cyan as every other PK film. The one permitted departure is warmth INSIDE the windows of the carried house - still within the teal family, a paler aqua glow - so the house reads as inhabited and worth carrying.
continuity: Every figure is back-to-camera and silhouetted. Faces never appear, at any point, no matter how many people are in frame.
Three motifs recur: the HOUSE (the bahay kubo on its bamboo poles), the LINE of figures, and HANDS on the poles.
The house must be the same house in every shot - stilted bamboo hut, steep thatched roof, one glowing window.
Shots marked chain:false open somewhere new and are generated without the previous frame as reference.
timing_note: 226s. At ~12s per still that is 19 shots for the stills render; at 8s per clip it is 29 for a Veo render. Written here as 24 shots, with trim:true marking the first to drop. The lyric timings available are the first 31s only - the full-audio pass must re-cut these against the real chorus positions, because the chorus (Sama-sama sa bawat hakbang) should always land on a shot where the count JUMPS.

shots.desc: Vast empty flooded rice terrace at dawn, mirror-still water, mountains behind. One small hooded figure stands dead centre, back to us. Nothing else in the frame.
The figure from behind, facing a small stilted bamboo house with a steep thatched roof and one softly glowing window. He does not move toward it.
One pair of hands closing around a bamboo pole beneath the house. The pole does not lift. The hands stay closed on it.
The figure straining alone against the pole, the house not moving at all. He is far too small for it. The scale is the point.
shots.camera: slow pull back to show how big the house is

shots.desc: A second identical hooded silhouette walks in from frame left and takes the other end of the same pole. Neither turns to the other.
Two pairs of hands now on the pole, spaced apart. The pole lifts a few inches clear of the ground.
Two more identical silhouettes wade in through the shallow water from opposite edges of frame, taking the two remaining corner poles.
Four figures, one at each corner, the house now fully off the ground and swaying slightly. Water drips from the poles.
A long line of identical hooded silhouettes wading in single file across the flooded terrace toward the house, reflections doubling them in the water.
shots.camera: slow lateral track along the line

shots.desc: Figures packing in shoulder to shoulder beneath the house, hands going up onto the poles one after another, filling every gap.
A dense row of hands gripping one bamboo pole, packed tight along its whole length, no space left on it.
shots.camera: slow lateral track along the pole

shots.desc: The house fully airborne, carried high on a crowd of identical silhouettes moving as one body across the water. Too many to count.
shots.camera: slow rise, revealing the scale of the crowd

shots.desc: The crowd from behind, walking away from camera, the house riding above their heads, one glowing window visible in it.
High and wide: the whole procession crossing an immense flooded plain, a single dark ribbon of figures under an enormous pale sky.
The sky darkens hard and rain comes down in sheets. The procession does not stop. The house tilts but stays up.
Hands slipping on a wet pole, then other hands closing over them, more hands than there is room for.
One figure stumbles and goes down into the water. Two others stop, turn back, and lift him. The line closes over the gap.
The procession pushing on through the downpour, the house still high, nobody left behind on the water behind them.
The rain breaks. Pale light opens across the water. The house is set down gently on new high ground.
Hands releasing the pole one by one, opening, falling away. The last hand lets go.
The crowd standing back from the house, all of them facing it, none facing us. The window glows warmer than before.
The crowd disperses in every direction across the water, each figure walking away alone, the house left standing behind them.
One figure alone again on the open water, back to us - the same framing as shot one, the same figure, the same stance.
shots.camera: very slow push in, echoing shot 1

shots.desc: Pull back from that lone figure to reveal he is one point in a line of identical silhouettes stretching past both edges of frame, all walking the same way. He was never alone.
shots.camera: long slow pull back, the reveal

status: PARKED Aug 25 2026 - Jordan reviewed the finished 3:45 render and did not like it. He is directing the next one himself. Everything below stands as a record of what was tried, not as an approved plan.
post_mortem: PACE IS THE PRIME SUSPECT. 24 stills across 225s is 9.4s per shot. The mini-movie standard Jordan liked is 2.75s. A Ken Burns push that reads as cinematic over 3s reads as a screensaver over 9. Fixing it means generating MORE stills, not stretching fewer - 45 shots at 5s, or 80 at 2.75s. Stills are free; only the render time grows.

The pipeline is direction-agnostic and is the part that now works: storyboard JSON -> storyboard_stills.py (free) -> movie_render_wide.py -> 1920x1080 non-Short. Changing the creative costs one JSON edit, a free regeneration, and ~20 unattended minutes.

What did work and is worth keeping: character consistency held across 24 separate generations; the count arc (1 -> 2 -> line -> crowd -> 1 -> line past the frame edges) was legible; the bilingual lyric treatment was correct once the Tagalog transcription was fixed.
UNRESOLVED, needs a Filipino ear: the chorus line is rendered 'Pagtutulungan, pagdadamayan'. An earlier transcript had 'Pagtutulungan kung dadamayan'. Not confirmed by Jordan.
